messages.author: f383ad53e3901131
messages.subject: Real-valued parameter for Poisson
parts:
Hi,

I read from the reference manual and previous posts in this group that the Poisson distribution does not support the declaration of a real-valued parameter. I converted a logistic growth JAGS model to STAN code as below. Lambda is calculated based on the parameters K,Q and b, which will cause it to be a real rather than an integer. This is then passed on to the Poisson distribution in the model block. I was wondering if there is any way to get around the integer declaration, please?

Any advice would be much appreciated!

Regards,
Cindy


#######################
###Model code for RSTAN
#######################

data {
int<lower=0> nobs;
int<lower=0> delta_D[nobs];
int<lower=0> delta_V[nobs];
int<lower=0> delta_W[nobs];
int<lower=0> delta_Z[nobs];
int<lower=0> T1[nobs];
int<lower=0> T2[nobs];
int<lower=0> pop;

}


parameters {
real alphaD;
real alphaV;
real alphaW;
real alphaZ;
real betaD;
real betaV;
real betaW;
real betaZ;

real muK;
real muQ;
real mub;

real<lower=0> sigmaK;
real<lower=0> sigmaQ;
real<lower=0> sigmab;

real thetaW;
real thetaK;
real thetaQ;
real thetab;

real <lower=0> I[nobs];

real<lower=0,upper=1> pD;
real<lower=0,upper=1> pV;
real<lower=0,upper=1> pW;
real<lower=0,upper=1> pZ;

}


transformed parameters {

real K;
real Q;
real b;
real lambda[nobs];
K<-exp(thetaK);
Q<-exp(thetaQ);
b<-exp(thetab);

for (j in 1:nobs)
{
lambda[j] <- 0.001 + (K/(Q*exp(-b*T2[j])+1))-(K/(Q*exp(-b*T1[j])+1));
}

}


model {

for (j in 1:nobs)
{
I[j] ~ poisson(pop*lambda[j]); 

delta_D[j] ~ binomial(I[j],pD);

delta_V[j] ~ binomial(I[j],pV); 

delta_Z[j] ~ binomial(I[j],pZ); 

delta_W[j] ~ poisson(thetaW*pW*I[j]);
}


thetaK ~ dnorm(muK,sigmaK);
thetaQ ~ dnorm(muQ,sigmaQ);
thetab ~ dnorm(mub,sigmab);

pD ~ dbeta(alphaD,betaD);
pV ~ dbeta(alphaV,betaV);
pZ ~ dbeta(alphaZ,betaZ);
pW ~ dbeta(alphaW,betaW);

alphaD ~ dexp(0.001);
alphaV ~ dexp(0.001);
alphaZ ~ dexp(0.001);
alphaW ~ dexp(0.001);

betaD ~ dexp(0.001);
betaV ~ dexp(0.001);
betaZ ~ dexp(0.001);
betaW ~ dexp(0.001);

thetaW ~ dunif(0,1000000);

muK ~ dnorm(0,0.0001);
muQ ~ dnorm(0,0.0001);
mub ~ dnorm(0,0.0001);

sigmaK ~ dunif(0,100);
sigmaQ ~ dunif(0,100);
sigmab ~ dunif(0,100);

}

messages.author: f13fe7e880ed6103
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Real-valued parameter for Poisson
parts:
Wait, are you asking about the parameter lambda or the data n?

The rate parameter of the Poisson distribution lambda can be real
(from the manual p. 356):

real poisson_log(ints n, reals lambda)
The log Poisson probability mass of n given rate lambda

It's the observations that are giving you trouble because they need to
be integer:
real <lower=0> I[nobs];

But that doesn't seem like it'll be a problem for your model, will it?
I don't have your data to try, but I think this should work:
int<lower=0> I[nobs];

Best,
Seth

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real-valued parameter for Poisson
parts:
Stan does not allow integer parameters and also does not
allow non-integer variables for Poisson. If you have

u ~ poisson(v);

then u must be an integer type, which means it can't be
a parameter.

The only way Stan can deal with models with discrete parameters
is by marginalizing them out.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real-valued parameter for Poisson
parts:
I don't think you're going to be able to fit a model with
missing integer data with a Poisson distribution in Stan.

It's one of the hard limitations on things we can't do that
you can do in BUGS or JAGS.

There's a chapter in the manual on latent discrete parameters
and how to marginalize them out and also examples in the
mixture modeling chapter.

Basically, if z are the discrete parameters and theta continuous
params and y data, then you can marginalize the joint prob
function

p(theta, y) = SUM_z p(theta, z, y)

and then take

p(theta | y) propto p(theta, y)

with Bayes's rule and you're good to go.

The problem is that it's an infinite sum for the Poisson.

- Bob

 x ~ poisson(mu);
 N ~ binomial(x,p);

2015年5月29日金曜日 2時20分22秒 UTC+9 Bob Carpenter:

I don't think you're going to be able to fit a model with
missing integer data with a Poisson distribution in Stan.

It's one of the hard limitations on things we can't do that
you can do in BUGS or JAGS.

There's a chapter in the manual on latent discrete parameters
and how to marginalize them out and also examples in the
mixture modeling chapter.

Basically, if z are the discrete parameters and theta continuous
params and y data, then you can marginalize the joint prob
function

   p(theta, y) = SUM_z p(theta, z, y)

and then take

  p(theta | y) propto p(theta, y)

with Bayes's rule and you're good to go.

The problem is that it's an infinite sum for the Poisson.

- Bob
